page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading, running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, providing 7.71 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Passmark memory benchmarks also rank in the top tier. However, multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls into the average tier. Large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 21.89 GB/sec, whereas read-only memory bandwidth remains average. Small-model LLM text generation is highly efficient, reaching top-tier speeds, while medium-model inference remains average.

Given its bare metal architecture, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial 3890 GB NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast DDR5 memory speed make it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and local storage-heavy operations. The strong single-core performance combined with average multi-core capabilities positions this server well for database operations, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, though it is less optimal for highly parallelized, write-heavy computing.
